title: Start here
description: Follow a parcel from satellite observations to an inspection decision.
input: Parcel geometries and a unique identifier; labels are needed for supervised classification.
output: Parcel features, diagnostic reports, predictions and inspection priorities.
steps: Prepare your parcels
Upload and inspect a GeoPackage, GeoParquet or GeoJSON; select its layer and unique parcel ID.
Acquire and summarize observations
openEO retrieves imagery. Local processing turns cleaned pixels into one row per parcel.
Understand and classify
EDA describes the data. ML trains and evaluates models, then predicts every row.
Review the evidence
Use confidence, reliability and inspection rules to prioritize human review.

title: openEO acquisition
description: Plan the spatial work and acquire Sentinel observations through Copernicus.
input: Parcel geometries, dates, Sentinel settings and Copernicus accounts.
output: Downloaded raster cubes ready for local processing.
steps: Configure inputs and accounts
Choose parcels, dates, bands, cloud masking and the accounts that will execute remote jobs.
Plan partitions and batches
Split the input into outer partitions, then plan buffered or tile-based remote batches.
Build Sentinel cubes
Acquire Sentinel-2 and/or Sentinel-1 observations, with the configured masking, resampling and temporal behavior.
Schedule, monitor and download
Submit jobs, apply the retry policy and download completed cubes. Remote completion is only one stage of the run.

title: Parcel statistics
description: Turn downloaded raster cubes into quality-aware parcel features.
input: Downloaded cubes, parcel geometries and local processing settings.
output: Dated and reduced GeoParquet tables, cleaning reports and completion records.
steps: Open and validate each cube
Check physical bands, coordinates and coverage before local calculation.
Clean and fill physical bands
Apply configured IQR cleaning and observation checks, then temporal filling before spatial filling and interpolation.
Calculate indices
Derive spectral indices from the cleaned physical bands and preserve observed-versus-filled provenance.
Aggregate parcel pixels
Mask pixels by parcel, calculate the selected statistics, and reshape dated values into one row per parcel.
Persist and publish results
Assemble parcel tables and cleaning reports. Completion is recorded after the required outputs are saved and verified.
articles: Local processing, quality counts and checkpoints
Parcel statistics API and output files

title: Feature enrichment
description: Optional enrichment for Python and notebook workflows.
input: A parcel feature table and any required environmental reference datasets.
output: A parcel table with temporal summaries or environmental attributes.
steps: Reduce dated features
Summarize observations over time when appropriate. The statistics pipeline already writes a reduced sibling table.
Add environmental context
Optional functions add elevation, soil and nearest-lake features from separately supplied reference data.
Choose the analysis table
Keep one row per parcel and retain ID, target and geometry roles for downstream analysis.
articles: Available features and where to use them

title: EDA
description: Understand data quality, relationships and candidate features before training.
input: A completed parcel-statistics result in the app, plus chosen column roles and EDA settings.
output: Diagnostic tables, plots, annotated rows, an HTML report and an initial feature proposal.
steps: Validate and profile
Validate configuration, prepare the output folder, identify column types and summarize missingness and distributions.
Calculate statistical evidence
Measure feature relationships and target-dependent associations where labels are available.
Screen candidate features
Apply quality, association, redundancy and stability gates to form an exploratory proposal.
Run multivariate diagnostics
Calculate configured VIF, PCA and outlier diagnostics, then annotate input rows.
Write artifacts and report
Generate plots, save diagnostic tables and render the HTML report. Final feature selection requires train-only validation.

title: ML classification
description: Run a reproducible classification scenario in five restartable steps.
input: A completed EDA analysis in the app, selected features and a target with labelled rows.
output: Saved models, evaluation reports, predictions, probabilities and inspection evidence.
steps: Check
Validate input, feature and target roles; record diagnostics and prepare the run artifacts.
Prepare
Build the training/test split and cross-validation folds, optionally using spatial separation.
Train
Tune selected classifiers using training data and cross-validation.
Evaluate
Evaluate the candidate models and configured prediction strategies; persist the selected strategy.
Predict
Refit and predict all rows, including unlabelled parcels, then calculate confidence and inspection evidence.

title: Inspection
description: Understand how prediction evidence becomes a human review priority.
input: Predictions, declared labels, confidence, class reliability, geometry and available quality diagnostics.
output: Inspection priorities and a ranked review queue; these support human decisions.
steps: Calculate confidence and reliability
Combine model evidence, rank-based confidence and class reliability diagnostics.
Apply the decision rules
Compare predictions with declarations and assess data and geometry reliability.
Apply optional outlier adjustment
Use EDA outlier evidence when configured. EDA is required before ML in the app, but this adjustment is optional.
Review the prioritized parcels
Inspect the reasons and evidence behind each priority rather than treating priority as a probability.
assets: Detailed inspection evidence and all decision rules

title: Advanced reference
description: Setup, command-line use and implementation details for technical readers.
input: The workflow you want to configure, operate or extend.
output: Practical setup instructions and the source ownership map.
